behaviors.behavior: AC1: AC ids are minted by a tool (mint()), in document order, zero-padded, never hand-typed
AC1: the minting CLI (mint_ac_ids.py) dry-runs by default and only writes under --write
AC2: read()/read_all() parse the shipped FR heading+bullet shape and pair each criterion with its minted id
AC2: read() composes on lib.fr_criteria (R0) for continuation-line joining rather than reimplementing it
AC2: golden corpus pins boundary shapes for BOTH mint() and read(), round-tripped
AC2: read()/read_all() agree with mint() on scope -- neither scans the legacy bold-anchor form
AC3: re-running the minter on its own output is a no-op (idempotent)
AC3: inserting a bullet in the middle never renumbers existing ids
AC3: deleting a minted bullet never frees its number; stale/ahead registry self-heals
An untrustworthy marker (non-canonical digits, [AC00], near-miss shapes, stacked, duplicate) is rejected loudly
A negative/non-int registry value is rejected by the CLI and by mint() itself
A duplicate-marker document makes the CLI exit non-zero
Concurrent --write invocations are serialized by a file lock
behaviors.evidence: exercised by every CLI subprocess test via mint_ac_ids.py's file_lock()

behaviors.behavior: --write persists the registry before the spec (harmless-gap-not-reuse ordering)
behaviors.evidence: test_write_creates_the_registry_file_even_when_the_spec_has_no_bullets PASSED; ordering itself recorded in the ADR

surface_verification.justification: P3.1 is dormant infrastructure (SPEC S8 E1 / S5 no downstream effect) -- a pure Python library and CLI tool with no startable web/dev-server surface of its own and not wired into any consumer yet; the golden-corpus unit tests and CLI subprocess tests are the verification.
